intent: Portable profile path, study vars, slugify/essay_window macros, and enrichment seeds (labs, release-type map, tier map, source hierarchy, date sensitivity)

edits.new_content:
pace_the_frontier:
  target: dev
  outputs:
    dev:
      type: duckdb
      # Relative to this project directory: dbt (and dex) run with cwd = pace_the_frontier/.
      path: ../warehouse/pace_the_frontier.duckdb

name: pace_the_frontier
version: 1.0.0
profile: pace_the_frontier
model-paths:
- models
seed-paths:
- seeds
test-paths:
- tests
macro-paths:
- macros
vars:
  # Publication date of "We Must Pace the Frontier" (METHODOLOGY section 3).
  essay_date: '2026-09-12'
  # Width of each comparison window in calendar days, excluding the essay day.
  window_days: 30
models:
  pace_the_frontier:
    staging:
      +schema: staging
      +materialized: view
    intermediate:
      +schema: intermediate
      +materialized: view
    marts:
      +schema: marts
      +materialized: table
seeds:
  pace_the_frontier:
    +schema: reference

{#- Classify a signed day offset from the essay date into the study windows
    (METHODOLOGY section 3): before = -30..-1, after = +1..+30, the essay day
    itself belongs to neither window, everything else is outside. -#}
{% macro essay_window(days_expression) -%}
    case
        when {{ days_expression }} between -{{ var('window_days') }} and -1 then 'before'
        when {{ days_expression }} between 1 and {{ var('window_days') }} then 'after'
        when {{ days_expression }} = 0 then 'essay_day'
        else 'outside'
    end
{%- endmacro %}

version: 2

seeds:
  - name: seed_labs
    description: >
      One row per lab that appears in the research, the 13 labs on the agreed list plus the
      four borderline labs (METHODOLOGY 4.1). Country and region are general knowledge.
      Essay stance comes only from sources the study already cites: the essay itself and
      NYU Shanghai RITS (15 Sep 2026), which reports the Altman and Musk endorsements.
      `none_recorded` means no response was found in those sources; it was not researched
      further and is not evidence of disagreement.
    config:
      column_types:
        in_scope_list: boolean
        stance_date: date
    columns:
      - name: lab_id
        description: Slug of the lab name; matches `slugify(developer)` in staging.
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: lab_name
        description: Lab name exactly as written in the research CSV `developer` column.
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: in_scope_list
        description: True for the 13 labs on the agreed list (METHODOLOGY 4.1), false for borderline labs.
        data_tests: [not_null]
      - name: parent_country
        description: Country of the lab's parent company.
      - name: region
        description: US, China, Europe or Japan.
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: [US, China, Europe, Japan]
      - name: essay_coordination_group
        description: >
          Where the lab sits relative to the essay's asks. `us_frontier_company`: covered by the
          proposed US regulation and the democratic coordination talks. `other_democracy`: in
          scope for democratic coordination only. `china`: reached only by the essay's global
          coordination levels.
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: [us_frontier_company, other_democracy, china]
      - name: essay_stance
        description: author, endorsed_publicly or none_recorded (see model description).
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: [author, endorsed_publicly, none_recorded]
      - name: stance_date
        description: Date of the public stance, when one is recorded.
      - name: stance_quote
        description: Verbatim public statement, when one is recorded.
      - name: stance_source_url
        description: Source for the stance.

  - name: seed_release_type_map
    description: >
      Maps each distinct `release_type` string in the research CSV to normalized access
      attributes. Derived only from the wording of `release_type`. Access level describes
      access on the counted (first-announcement) date.
    config:
      column_types:
        has_gated_variant: boolean
        is_snapshot_update: boolean
        is_staggered_rollout: boolean
    columns:
      - name: release_type
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: access_level
        description: >
          general_availability (anyone can use it through an API, app or weights),
          preview_or_limited (a preview, experimental build, or a single product surface such as
          one coding tool or a subscription plan), gated_or_restricted (access by vetting or a
          trusted-access program), announced_only, cancelled, non_release (pricing or serving
          tiers, configurations and roadmap mentions, all excluded rows).
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: [general_availability, preview_or_limited, gated_or_restricted, announced_only, cancelled, non_release]
      - name: open_weights_status
        description: at_launch, promised_later (weights announced for a later date) or none.
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: [at_launch, promised_later, none]
      - name: has_gated_variant
        description: The same model also shipped at a restricted access level (Mythos, Gemini Flash Cyber).
      - name: is_snapshot_update
        description: The release type names a point release or snapshot update of an existing model.
      - name: is_staggered_rollout
        description: The release type names later dates for wider access or weights.

  - name: seed_tier_map
    description: Maps each distinct `tier` string to a coarse tier band and rank (1 = flagship).
    columns:
      - name: tier
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: tier_band
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: [flagship, upper, mid, small_fast]
      - name: tier_rank
        description: 1 flagship, 2 upper, 3 mid, 4 small or fast.

  - name: seed_source_domains
    description: >
      Maps each `source_url` domain to the source hierarchy in METHODOLOGY section 5:
      1 vendor, 2 tracker citing vendor primaries, 3 trade press, 4 aggregator listing.
    columns:
      - name: source_domain
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: source_type
        data_tests:
          - accepted_values:
              arguments:
                values: [vendor, tracker, press, aggregator]
      - name: source_rank

  - name: seed_date_sensitivity
    description: >
      The rows whose date is disputed between credible sources, transcribed from
      METHODOLOGY section 7.1. Used to rebuild the windows under the conflicting dates.
    config:
      column_types:
        date_used: date
        conflicting_date: date
    columns:
      - name: model_name
        data_tests: [unique, not_null]
      - name: date_used
      - name: conflicting_date
      - name: conflicting_date_source
